nodes.summary: Declares the ActivityEntry type (title, optional amount and status, and a showAmount flag) that the home page builds from transfers and that RecentActivity and ActivityList pass down to render activity rows.

nodes.name: CustomBalanceCard.tsx
nodes.summary: Shared MUI Card component that shows an icon and label row above a right-aligned large numeric value, and swaps the value for a CircularProgress spinner while isLoading is true; TokenBalance and WalletBalance build on it.

nodes.name: SnackbarContext.tsx
nodes.summary: React context module that holds the transaction-snackbar state (an open flag and the last send or request transaction) and exposes show, hide, and undo actions through SnackbarProvider and the useSnackbar hook; undo only logs and clears the state, with no API call yet.
nodes.languageNotes: The context is created with an undefined default, so useSnackbar can detect a missing SnackbarProvider and throw a clear error instead of returning silent no-op values.

nodes.name: toActivityEntry
nodes.summary: Converts a wallet-api Transfer into an ActivityEntry: it treats the transfer as sent when the source wallet is in the user's wallet-name set, builds a 'Sent to X' or 'Received from X' title, negates the amount for sent transfers, maps the state to Pending, Sent, Received, Cancelled, Failed, or Unknown, and shows the amount only for completed transfers.

nodes.name: Page
nodes.summary: Default-exported home page component that sums tokens_in_wallet and tokens_pending across wallets, memoizes the wallet-name set and the mapped activity list, reads and clears sessionStorage 'pendingTransaction' on mount to open the snackbar, and renders TokenBalance, WalletBalance, RecentActivity, and TransactionSnackbar.

nodes.name: ActivityList
nodes.summary: Renders each ActivityEntry as an ActivityItem inside an MUI Box, keyed by array index, and forwards the title, amount, status, and showAmount props of each entry.

nodes.name: RecentActivity
nodes.summary: Function component that takes activityData and an optional isLoading flag (default false) and shows one of three states under the section header: three 64px rounded skeletons, a 'No recent activity yet' message, or the ActivityList.

nodes.name: TokenBalance
nodes.summary: Function component that accepts tokenCount, an optional pendingCount (default 0), and isLoading, and passes a TollOutlined icon and a pending-aware 'Tokens' label to CustomBalanceCard.

nodes.name: TransactionSnackbar
nodes.summary: Function component that takes open, transaction, onClose, and onUndo props and renders a bottom-centered Snackbar whose Alert reports the token amount and whether it was sent or requested, with a green UNDO action button wired to onUndo.

nodes.name: WalletBalance
nodes.summary: Function component that accepts walletAmount and isLoading and forwards them to CustomBalanceCard with the fixed 'Wallet' label and an AccountBalanceWalletOutlined icon.

nodes.name: CustomBalanceCard
nodes.summary: Function component that takes icon, label, value, and isLoading (default false) props and lays them out in a flex Card with a 45 percent minimum width, showing a 28px spinner in place of the h4 value while loading.

nodes.name: SnackbarProvider
nodes.summary: Context provider component that keeps snackbarOpen and lastTransaction in useState and gives its children showTransactionSnackbar (store and open), hideSnackbar (close), and undoTransaction (log, close, and clear); the (protected) layout imports this module.

nodes.name: useSnackbar
nodes.summary: Custom hook that reads SnackbarContext with useContext and throws 'useSnackbar must be used within a SnackbarProvider' when no provider is present; the home Page uses it to drive TransactionSnackbar.

nodes.name: WalletCreateDrawer.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test suite for WalletCreateDrawer that mounts it with spied onClose and onCreate props and checks open/closed rendering, the Create Wallet enable rule, trimmed payloads, case-insensitive duplicate-name errors, API rejection messages, stale errors after close, and the discard-changes dialog.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a local Harness component with React.useState and a captured Promise reject callback to simulate a create request that fails after the drawer closes.

nodes.name: WalletItem.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test suite for WalletItem that mounts it with sample names, created_at dates, and token counts, and asserts that the name, balance, date, and zero balance render and that the 'N pending' caption appears only when tokens_pending is non-zero.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Next.js client page at /wallet/customize that loads the wallet named in the ?name query, lets the user edit display name and about text and upload logo and hero images (1MB max, image/* only), then saves through useUpdateWallet and hard-reloads /wallet/details after 2 seconds.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses window.location.assign instead of router.push after a save so that useGetWallets refetches fresh data; image previews come from FileReader.readAsDataURL.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Next.js client page at /wallet/details that shows one wallet's cover, logo, display name, about text, balance with pending count, a web-map link built from NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_URL, and its token list from useGetTokens, and opens WalletProfileDrawer to PATCH the profile and reload the wallets.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps the useSearchParams consumer in a Suspense boundary, as the Next.js App Router expects for client search-param reads, and memoizes initialProfile so loading-state changes do not reset an open drawer.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Next.js client page at /wallet that lists the user's wallets as WalletItem rows linking to /wallet/details, enforces a client-side limit of 2 wallets, creates wallets through WalletCreateDrawer, and then redeems any pending claim link into the new wallet via claimPendingToken.

nodes.name: GenericDrawer.tsx
nodes.summary: Reusable MUI bottom Drawer with rounded top corners, a title row, and a close icon button that renders arbitrary children; the /wallet page uses it for the Good-to-know info panel.

nodes.name: WalletCreateDrawer.tsx
nodes.summary: Bottom-drawer form for creating a wallet with required name and description fields, case-insensitive duplicate-name detection against existingNames, async onCreate submission that maps API error messages to the field they concern, and a discard-changes confirmation dialog for dirty closes.
nodes.languageNotes: Resets all local state in a useEffect keyed on the open prop, so an error from a request that settles after the drawer closes is cleared on the next open.

nodes.name: WalletItem.tsx
nodes.summary: Presentational wallet row card that shows a logo Avatar with an initial-letter fallback, the wallet name and created_at date, the token balance, and an 'N pending' caption when tokens_pending is non-zero; the /wallet page renders one per wallet.

nodes.name: WalletProfileDrawer.tsx
nodes.summary: Bottom-drawer form for editing a wallet profile's display name (2-30 chars), about text (5-250 chars), and public web-map visibility; it seeds the fields from the initial prop on open, validates with walletFieldError, and passes a WalletProfileUpdate to the async onSave prop.

nodes.name: CustomTextField.tsx
nodes.summary: Memoized MUI filled text input wrapper that exposes label, type, helper text, error, ref, and data-test id props, adds a show/hide password toggle, and sets autoComplete from the type; the wallet create and profile drawers use it for their fields.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapped in React.memo with an explicit displayName so that the memoized component keeps a readable name in React DevTools.

nodes.name: plainText.ts
nodes.summary: Utility module that converts legacy HTML wallet about text to plain text by stripping tags, decoding six common HTML entities, and trimming; the customize page, the details page, and WalletProfileDrawer use it.

nodes.name: walletFields.ts
nodes.summary: Utility module that validates an editable wallet profile field against the API patch rules: it forbids emptying a field that loaded with a value and enforces a min-max character length; the customize page and WalletProfileDrawer use it.

nodes.name: CustomizeWallet
nodes.summary: Client component that resolves the wallet by the name query param, seeds display name, about, and image previews from it, checks file size and MIME type for logo and hero uploads, and calls updateWallet with fields plus logo_image and cover_image before it redirects to the details page.

nodes.name: CustomizeWalletPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported Next.js page component for the /wallet/customize route that only renders CustomizeWallet, with no Suspense boundary around its useSearchParams call.

nodes.name: WalletDetails
nodes.summary: Client component that reads the wallet name from the URL, loads tokens and wallets, renders the wallet header, about text, balance and pending-transfer note, and clickable token rows to /token/details, and saves profile edits through updateWallet followed by reload.

nodes.name: WalletDetailsPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported Next.js page component for /wallet/details that wraps WalletDetails in a Suspense boundary with a 'Loading…' fallback box.

nodes.name: WalletPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported page component that mirrors server wallets into local state, handles wallet creation with an optimistic list prepend and a first-wallet gift notification, calls claimPendingToken with the auth token from tokenAtom, and renders the list, limit notice, info drawer, create drawer, and Snackbar.

nodes.name: GenericDrawer
nodes.summary: Component that renders an MUI Drawer anchored to the bottom with the given title, a close button bound to onClose, and its children inside padded content with a 164px minimum height.

nodes.name: WalletCreateDrawer
nodes.summary: React.FC that holds name, description, submitting, confirm, and submit-error state, enables Create Wallet only for a non-blank unique name with a description, awaits onCreate with trimmed values and then closes, and routes rejection messages to the name, description, or form error slot.

nodes.name: WalletItem
nodes.summary: Function component that takes name, created_at, tokens_in_wallet, tokens_pending, and logo_url props and renders them in an MUI Paper with data-test ids keyed by wallet name and a chevron button.

nodes.name: WalletProfileDrawer
nodes.summary: React.FC that resets its form from initial each time open becomes true, computes display name and about errors, builds a WalletProfileUpdate with add_to_web_map and the trimmed non-empty fields, awaits onSave, and shows the error message if the save rejects.

nodes.name: CustomTextField
nodes.summary: Memoized function component that renders FormControl, InputLabel, and FilledInput with an id derived from name, toggles password visibility through an end adornment, and shows non-blank helperText as a red FormHelperText tagged error-helper-text.

nodes.name: toPlainText
nodes.summary: Arrow function that removes all <...> tags from a string with a regex, replaces  , &, <, >, ", and ' with their characters from the ENTITIES map, and returns the trimmed result.

nodes.name: walletFieldError
nodes.summary: Returns '<label> cannot be emptied.' when the loaded value was non-blank and the trimmed current value is blank, 'Must be min-max characters.' when the length is out of range, and undefined otherwise.

nodes.name: accountConfirmation.tsx
nodes.summary: Expo Router screen at the /accountConfirmation route that tells a new user the account is created, shows a green check icon from Colors.green, and explains that a wallet is issued automatically. It composes ThemedSafeAreaView, ThemedStatusBar, ThemedView, ThemedText and Button with a local StyleSheet.
nodes.languageNotes: Expo Router maps the file name to the route, so the default export name Index does not affect the URL.

nodes.name: Index
nodes.summary: Default-export screen component that renders the 'Account created!' title, a check-mark circle, welcome and wallet text, and a CONTINUE Button. The Button onPress calls handleGoTo, which is still an empty stub, so the button does not navigate yet.

nodes.name: Button.tsx
nodes.summary: Shared primary action button for the native app: a full-width green (#61892F) TouchableOpacity with a white bold ThemedText label. It exports the Button component and its ButtonProps type (onPress, title), and the account confirmation screen uses it.

nodes.name: Button
nodes.summary: Renders a TouchableOpacity with activeOpacity 0.87 that calls the onPress prop and shows the title prop as a 'title' type ThemedText overridden to 20px bold white text.

nodes.name: Collapsible.tsx
nodes.summary: Expandable section component from the Expo starter template that toggles its children under a chevron heading, with the icon color taken from Colors.light.icon or Colors.dark.icon. No screen in the native app imports it at present.

nodes.name: Collapsible
nodes.summary: Keeps an isOpen state, renders a TouchableOpacity heading with an Ionicons chevron and a defaultSemiBold ThemedText title, and shows the children in an indented ThemedView only when isOpen is true.

nodes.name: ParallaxScrollView.tsx
nodes.summary: Expo starter template scroll container that puts a 250px header image above themed content and animates the header with react-native-reanimated as the user scrolls. No screen in the native app imports it at present.
nodes.languageNotes: useAnimatedStyle and interpolate run on the UI thread as Reanimated worklets, so the parallax effect does not block the JS thread.

nodes.name: ParallaxScrollView
nodes.summary: Takes headerImage, headerBackgroundColor (dark and light values) and children, tracks the scroll offset with useScrollViewOffset, and interpolates the header translateY and scale (zoom to 2x on overscroll) inside an Animated.ScrollView wrapped in ThemedView.

nodes.name: ThemeSafeArea.tsx
nodes.summary: Theme-aware SafeAreaView wrapper that the account confirmation screen imports to get the theme 'background' color plus safe-area insets. Its content is identical to ThemedSafeArea.tsx, so the two files are duplicates.

nodes.name: ThemedSafeAreaView
nodes.summary: Resolves the background color through useThemeColor with the optional lightColor and darkColor overrides and renders a react-native SafeAreaView with that background merged before the required style prop. accountConfirmation.tsx uses this copy.

nodes.name: ThemedSafeArea.tsx
nodes.summary: Duplicate copy of ThemeSafeArea.tsx that exports the same ThemedSafeAreaView component and ThemedSafeAreaViewProps type. No file in the native app imports this copy, so it is a candidate for removal.

nodes.name: ThemedSafeAreaView
nodes.summary: Unused duplicate of the ThemeSafeArea.tsx component: it calls useThemeColor for the 'background' color and renders a SafeAreaView with that color and the caller style, forwarding the other ViewProps.

nodes.name: ThemedStatusBar.tsx
nodes.summary: Status bar wrapper that picks the status bar text style from the props instead of from the active color scheme. The account confirmation screen renders it without props, so that screen gets dark-content.

nodes.name: ThemedStatusBar
nodes.summary: Renders a react-native StatusBar with barStyle 'light-content' when a darkColor prop is present and 'dark-content' otherwise, and forwards the other StatusBarProps. The lightColor prop is accepted but not used.

nodes.name: ThemedText.tsx
nodes.summary: Theme-aware Text primitive for the native app that maps a type variant (default, title, defaultSemiBold, subtitle, link) to a Roboto StyleSheet entry. Button, Collapsible, the account confirmation screen and the auth screens (login, forgotPassword, checkEmail) use it, and ThemedText-test.tsx snapshots it.

nodes.name: ThemedText
nodes.summary: Gets the 'text' color from useThemeColor (with the lightColor and darkColor overrides), then renders a react-native Text whose style array is the color, the style for the chosen type (default 'default'), and the caller style last.

nodes.name: ThemedView.tsx
nodes.summary: Theme-aware View primitive that paints the theme 'background' color behind its children. Collapsible, ParallaxScrollView and the account confirmation screen use it as their themed container.

nodes.name: ThemedView
nodes.summary: Calls useThemeColor for the 'background' key with the optional lightColor and darkColor overrides and renders a react-native View with that background color before the caller style, forwarding the other ViewProps.

nodes.name: ThemedText-test.tsx
nodes.summary: Jest snapshot test that renders <ThemedText>Snapshot test!</ThemedText> with react-test-renderer and compares the JSON tree to the stored snapshot. It is the only test in this batch and covers the ThemedText default style path.

nodes.name: useThemeColor.ts
nodes.summary: Theme color hook from the Expo starter pattern that reads the device color scheme and returns either a caller override or the matching entry of the Colors palette in constants/Colors.ts. ThemedText, ThemedView and both ThemedSafeAreaView copies call it.

nodes.name: useThemeColor
nodes.summary: Takes a { light?, dark? } override object and a colorName key that exists in both Colors.light and Colors.dark, uses useColorScheme (default 'light'), and returns the override for the active theme or else Colors[theme][colorName].

nodes.name: loadingAtom.ts
nodes.summary: Declares loadingAtom, a Jotai primitive boolean atom that starts as true and tracks whether an auth request is in flight; loginAtom and registerAtom set it true before their fetch and false in their finally block.

nodes.name: loginAtom.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the write-only Jotai loginAtom that trims and Joi-validates login form values, then POSTs them to the treetracker user API /login endpoint with cookie credentials and returns the response data or an error object.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Jotai write-only atom pattern atom(null, async (get, set, args) => ...), so components trigger the action with useSetAtom and await its returned result.

nodes.name: loginAtom
nodes.summary: Async write handler that runs trimInputs and loginSchema.validate with abortEarly false, returns fieldErrors from handleValidationError on failure, otherwise fetches POST /login, returns the JSON body on success or the server message, and resets loadingAtom in finally.

nodes.name: logoutAtom.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the write-only Jotai logoutAtom that clears the session by setting tokenAtom to null; it imports loadingAtom but never uses it and makes no server call.

nodes.name: registerAtom.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the write-only Jotai registerAtom that trims and Joi-validates sign-up form values, then POSTs them to the treetracker user API /register endpoint and returns a success payload or an error object.

nodes.name: registerAtom
nodes.summary: Async write handler that validates trimmed form values against registerSchema, returns per-field errors on failure, otherwise fetches POST /register with credentials and returns success true plus the server message and data, toggling loadingAtom around the request.

nodes.name: tokenAtom.ts
nodes.summary: Declares tokenAtom, a persisted Jotai atomWithStorage under the key "token" that holds the auth token string or null, backed by a JSON storage built from getAsyncStorage so it uses sessionStorage on web and AsyncStorage on native.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: One-line barrel that re-exports everything from ./authSchemas, giving loginAtom and registerAtom a single import path for loginSchema and registerSchema.

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: Exports the User interface that types auth form state: a required password, optional username, name and email fields, and UI flags for submission status, a general error, and a fieldErrors map.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves and exports TREETRACKER_USER_API, the user API base URL, from NEXT_PUBLIC_TREETRACKER_USER_API on web or from expo-constants extra.apiBaseUrl on React Native, defaulting to an empty string.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a runtime require of expo-constants inside the native branch so the web bundle does not need the Expo package; it repeats the isNative check from platform.ts instead of importing it.

nodes.name: platform.ts
nodes.summary: Exports the isNative flag, which is true when navigator.product equals ReactNative; storage.ts uses it to pick the web or native storage backend.

nodes.name: storage.ts
nodes.summary: Provides getAsyncStorage, a platform-aware factory for the Jotai AsyncStringStorage contract that tokenAtom uses to persist the auth token across web and mobile.

nodes.name: getAsyncStorage
nodes.summary: Returns an AsyncStringStorage that wraps window.sessionStorage in Promise-returning getItem, setItem and removeItem on web, or lazily requires @react-native-async-storage and delegates to it when isNative is true.

nodes.name: validation.ts
nodes.summary: Holds form helpers shared by loginAtom and registerAtom: trimInputs to clean User field strings before Joi validation and handleValidationError to turn Joi error details into a field-to-message map.

nodes.name: trimInputs
nodes.summary: Copies each key of a Partial<User> into a new object, calling trim() on string values and passing other values unchanged, and returns the result cast to User.

nodes.name: handleValidationError
nodes.summary: Reduces a Joi ValidationError details array into an object keyed by context.key with each detail message, skipping entries without a key, so the UI can show per-field errors.

nodes.name: share-token.steps.ts
nodes.summary: WebdriverIO Cucumber step definitions for the share-token.feature BDD: a seeded sender logs in through Keycloak, sends a token with 'share by QR code' enabled, and a fresh visitor opens the claim link, registers, creates a wallet, and sees the shared token redeemed into it. Uses seed.ts helpers to create and reset the Keycloak accounts, wallets, and token rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Scenario state (sharedTokenId, sharedLink, receiverWallet) lives in module-level variables shared across Given/When/Then callbacks.

nodes.name: clearSession
nodes.summary: Simulates a brand-new browser by visiting the Keycloak well-known URL to drop its SSO cookie, then loading the app /login page and clearing sessionStorage, localStorage, and all cookies. Used by loginAs and by the step where user A opens the share link.

nodes.name: keycloakLogin
nodes.summary: Fills the Keycloak hosted login form (#username, #password), clicks #kc-login, and waits up to 30 s for the app's navigation-home element to confirm a logged-in state.

nodes.name: registerAs
nodes.summary: Completes the Keycloak hosted registration form for a given email (username is the email local-part, fixed Share/Receiver names), tries several submit-button selectors with a JS click fallback, and waits for the app home navigation to appear.

nodes.name: createWalletUI
nodes.summary: Opens the /wallet page, clicks the wallet-create-open button, types the wallet name and a 'desc' description into the create form, and submits it, driving wallet creation through the web UI.

nodes.name: seed.ts
nodes.summary: Test-data seeding helpers for the BDD suite that delete and recreate fixed Keycloak users, wallets, and tokens so each run starts deterministic. Combines the @treetracker/keycloak admin API functions with direct Postgres (pg) writes to the wallet schema, because wallet-api has no delete endpoint; consumed by share-token.steps.ts.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports package api files by subpath (not the package index) to avoid pulling React hooks and jotai into a plain Node tsx context. createWallet and getTokens are imported but not used in the current code.

nodes.name: userToken
nodes.summary: Mints an end-user access token through the Keycloak direct password grant against the realm token endpoint with the public client id, and throws when the response has no access_token. Called by tokenFor.

nodes.name: createWalletInDB
nodes.summary: Opens a pg client, sets the wallet schema search_path, and inserts a wallet row for a Keycloak account id and name, returning the new wallet id. Called by seedAccount to bypass wallet-api and the gift poll.

nodes.name: createTokenInDB
nodes.summary: Picks one public.trees row with a uuid and no token_id, then inserts a token row with a random UUID linked to that capture and to the given wallet, returning the token id. Called by seedAccount when requireToken is true.

nodes.name: findUserId
nodes.summary: Queries the Keycloak admin users endpoint with an exact username match using an admin bearer token and returns the first user id, or null when no user exists. Used by seedAccount and resetAccount.

nodes.name: deleteWalletByName
nodes.summary: Wipes a wallet by its globally unique name in FK-safe order: deletes wallet_trust_log, wallet_trust, transaction, transfer, and wallet_event rows, re-homes its tokens to SENDER_WALLET_ID (or deletes them when unset), then deletes the wallet row.

nodes.name: seedAccount
nodes.summary: Resets and recreates a SeededAccount: gets an admin token, deletes any existing Keycloak user and same-named wallet, creates the Keycloak user via createUser, looks up its id, inserts the wallet in the DB, and optionally inserts a token. Called by the share-token Given step.

nodes.name: tokenFor
nodes.summary: Returns a fresh end-user access token for an already-seeded account by delegating to userToken with the account email and password.

nodes.name: seedTokenIntoWalletByName
nodes.summary: Polls up to 15 s for a wallet row by name, frees a fixed token id (deleting old token and transaction rows) when one is given, then inserts a non-pending token with a random capture_id into that wallet and returns its id.

nodes.name: resetAccount
nodes.summary: Deletes every Keycloak user that matches an email (by email query and by username) using an admin token, and optionally wipes the named wallet, so a UI-registered recipient can register again on re-runs. Called by the share-token registration step.

nodes.name: createAccountFromKeycloak.ts
nodes.summary: Keycloak admin API helper that creates a realm user with a non-temporary password credential, falling back to an exact-username lookup when Keycloak returns 409 Conflict. Used by the BDD seed utility and the keycloak e2e test.

nodes.name: createUser
nodes.summary: POSTs a user (username, email, names, enabled, password credential) to the Keycloak admin users endpoint with a bearer token and returns the new id parsed from the Location header; on 409 it searches by username and returns the existing id, otherwise throws.

nodes.name: deleteAccountFromKeycloak.ts
nodes.summary: Keycloak admin API helper module that deletes a realm user by id, built on axios and the shared Keycloak config values.

nodes.name: deleteAccountFromKeycloak
nodes.summary: Sends an axios DELETE to the Keycloak admin users/{userId} endpoint with a bearer token and returns the AxiosResponse; it rethrows axios errors with the server message or a default text. Called by seed.ts and the keycloak e2e test.

nodes.name: fetchTokenFromKeycloak.ts
nodes.summary: Keycloak service-account token fetcher that performs a client_credentials grant against the configured token URL. Supplies the admin token for the user create and delete helpers in seed.ts and in the keycloak e2e test.

nodes.name: fetchTokenFromKeycloak
nodes.summary: POSTs a client_credentials grant with the configured client id and secret to KEYCLOAK_TOKEN_URL and returns the access_token plus a tokenExpiresAt timestamp that is 10 s earlier than the reported expiry.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves the Keycloak base URL, realm, client id, client secret, and token URL for the keycloak package: it reads PRIVATE_KEYCLOAK_* env vars (via dotenv) on web and Node, and Expo Constants extra fields on React Native. Imported by all three Keycloak api helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Detects React Native with navigator.product and loads expo-constants through a runtime require so the web and Node bundles do not need it.

nodes.name: deleteAccount.spec.e2e.ts
nodes.summary: Jest end-to-end test for deleteAccountFromKeycloak against a live Keycloak: beforeAll fetches a client-credentials token and creates a testuser with a random password, and the test expects the delete call to return HTTP 204.

nodes.name: getTokens.ts
nodes.summary: Wallet package API module that lists the tokens in a named wallet through treetracker-wallet-api. Consumed by the useGetTokens hook and imported by the BDD seed utility.

nodes.name: getTokens
nodes.summary: Sends an axios GET to TREETRACKER_WALLET_API/tokens with the URL-encoded wallet name and a limit (default 100) and a bearer token, returns response.data ({ tokens }), and rethrows API errors with the server message.

nodes.name: useGetTokens.ts
nodes.summary: React hook module that loads the tokens of one wallet for the signed-in user, reading the auth token from the core tokenAtom (jotai) and calling getTokens.

nodes.name: useGetTokens
nodes.summary: React hook that reads the auth token from jotai tokenAtom and, when the token and wallet name are both set, calls getTokens in a useEffect; it returns { tokens, isTokensLoading, error } and re-runs when either input changes.

nodes.name: artifacts.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the BDD test-artifact directory layout under test-artifacts/ (per-PLATFORM reports, Cucumber JSON/HTML, videos, temp video area) plus helpers that slugify names, create screenshot folders, and embed recorded scenario MP4s into Cucumber JSON. Consumed by wdio.base.conf.ts and wdio.debug.conf.ts.

nodes.name: capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: Exports WebdriverIO capability arrays for four BDD targets: headless mobile-emulated Chrome (iPhone 390x844, classic WebDriver), a DevTools-enabled debug Chrome variant, an Appium UiAutomator2 Android emulator running the debug APK, and an Appium XCUITest iOS simulator.
nodes.languageNotes: Spreads a conditional array into Chrome args so HEADED=1 drops the --headless=new flag.

nodes.name: wdio.base.conf.ts
nodes.summary: Shared WebdriverIO Cucumber test-runner config (baseConfig) for the BDD suite: specs, timeouts, spec/video/cucumberjs-json reporters, and lifecycle hooks that reset artifact folders, add environment metadata, overlay step text on the page, save failure screenshots, and embed videos into the report on completion. Spread into the web, mobile, and debug configs.
nodes.languageNotes: Hook functions pass a closure to browser.execute, so that code runs inside the browser page, not in Node.

nodes.name: wdio.debug.conf.ts
nodes.summary: Debug WebdriverIO config that extends baseConfig with verbose logging, longer timeouts, the DevTools Chrome capability, and a chromedriver service that prefers the snap binary over the npm one. It replaces base artifact hooks with no-ops and adds afterSession cleanup that archives VideoReporter JSON and deletes per-worker frame caches.

nodes.name: wdio.mobile.conf.ts
nodes.summary: Mobile WebdriverIO config that extends baseConfig with one instance, longer timeouts, an Appium service on 127.0.0.1:4723, Android or iOS capabilities picked by the PLATFORM env var, and Cucumber filtering to @native scenarios.

nodes.name: wdio.web.conf.ts
nodes.summary: Web WebdriverIO config that extends baseConfig with the mobile-emulated Chrome capability, a Yarn-cache webdriver cacheDir, and Cucumber tag filter '@web and not @skip'; it relies on WebdriverIO v9 built-in driver management instead of a chromedriver service.

nodes.name: ensureDir
nodes.summary: Creates a directory and all missing parent directories with fs.mkdirSync recursive; used by scenarioDirs and associateVideos before writing artifacts.

nodes.name: slugify
nodes.summary: Turns a feature or scenario title into a lowercase hyphenated filesystem-safe slug by removing non-word characters and collapsing whitespace and repeated hyphens.

nodes.name: scenarioDirs
nodes.summary: Builds the per-scenario folder PLATFORM_VIDEOS_ROOT/<feature-slug>/<scenario-slug>, creates its screenshots subfolder, and returns both paths; the base config afterStep hook uses it to save failed-step PNGs.

nodes.name: canonical
nodes.summary: Normalizes a name to lowercase with runs of non-alphanumerics replaced by single hyphens and edge hyphens trimmed, so scenario titles compare equal to wdio-video-reporter file names.

nodes.name: matchVideoFile
nodes.summary: Finds an unused MP4 in VIDEOS_TMP whose canonical name equals or starts with the canonical scenario name, and returns the most recently modified candidate or null.

nodes.name: associateVideos
nodes.summary: Reads each Cucumber JSON report, matches every non-background scenario (longest name first) to its recorded MP4, copies the video to cucumber-html/videos/<feature>/<scenario>/run.mp4, and appends a base64 HTML <video> embedding to the last step. Writes the JSON back and returns the number of videos linked; called from the base config onComplete hook.

nodes.name: getEnvMetadata
nodes.summary: Maps a WebdriverIO capabilities object to report metadata: platform, browser, and browser version for browser sessions, or platform, device, OS version, and automation name for Appium sessions. The beforeSession hook adds the result to the cucumberjs-json report.

nodes.name: Welcome.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test that mounts the Welcome screen inside the MUI ThemeProvider with the app theme and checks the 'Account created!' heading, the welcome copy, the Continue button, the check-circle icon, and that clicking Continue calls a stubbed onContinue handler.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Next.js App Router client page for the protected /welcome route; it renders the Welcome component and sends the user to /home with the router when the user presses Continue.
nodes.languageNotes: The (protected) folder is a Next.js route group: it groups routes without adding a URL segment, so the page serves /welcome.

nodes.name: Page
nodes.summary: Default-exported page component that gets the Next.js router with useRouter and passes a handleContinue callback that pushes '/home' to the Welcome component as onContinue.

nodes.name: layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Root App Router layout for the web app; it wraps every page in the MUI AppRouterCacheProvider, the MUI ThemeProvider with the shared theme, CssBaseline, and the KeycloakProvider auth context, and paints the body with the theme background color.

nodes.name: RootLayout
nodes.summary: Default-exported root layout that renders the <html lang="en"> and <body> shell and nests props.children inside AppRouterCacheProvider (CSS layer enabled), ThemeProvider, CssBaseline, and KeycloakProvider.

nodes.name: ThemeProvider.tsx
nodes.summary: Client component module that offers a reusable MUI theme wrapper applying the shared app theme and CssBaseline; no file in the import data uses it, because layout.tsx sets up the MUI ThemeProvider directly.
nodes.languageNotes: The Container import is unused, and the file uses the global React namespace for types without importing React.

nodes.name: MUIThemeProvider
nodes.summary: Default-exported React.FC that renders its children inside the MUI ThemeProvider configured with the theme from theme.ts, together with a CssBaseline style reset.

nodes.name: Welcome.tsx
nodes.summary: Client component for the post-signup welcome screen: it shows an 'Account created!' heading, a check-circle icon in the custom header palette color, text about the reforestation mission and the automatic wallet, and a Continue button. The /welcome page uses it, and the Cypress component test covers it.

nodes.name: Welcome
nodes.summary: Default-exported component that takes an optional onContinue prop, reads the MUI theme with useTheme for the icon color, and lays out a centered full-height card whose Continue button calls onContinue only when the prop is set.

nodes.name: theme.ts
nodes.summary: Defines and default-exports the MUI theme for the web app: Greenstand green primary (#61892F), a custom 'header' palette color, a #f5f5f5 background, Roboto from next/font, a custom 'sub' typography variant, and style overrides for Alert, FilledInput, Button, and Link. layout.tsx, ThemeProvider.tsx, and the Welcome component test import it.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript module augmentation (declare module) to add the custom 'header' palette color and the 'sub' typography variant to the MUI types, so Typography and Link accept variant="sub" with type checking.

nodes.name: _layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Expo Router layout for the (tabs) group that declares the home, wallet, notifications, settings, and hidden search tab screens, renders them with CustomTabBar, and wraps them in a react-native-copilot CopilotProvider for the onboarding walkthrough.
nodes.languageNotes: File-based routing: Expo Router treats _layout.tsx as the navigator for its directory, and the parentheses in (tabs) make a route group that does not add a URL segment.

nodes.name: TabLayout
nodes.summary: Default-exported tab navigator component that hides headers, injects CustomTabBar through the tabBar prop, and sets href null on the search screen so that it is routable but not shown as a tab.

nodes.name: _layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Root Expo Router layout of the native app that keeps the splash screen visible until the Roboto fonts load, then renders the active route through Slot inside ModalProvider together with the global ActionSelectionModal.

nodes.name: AppLayout
nodes.summary: Root layout component that loads Roboto_400Regular and Roboto_500Medium with useFonts, hides the splash screen on load success or error, and mounts ModalProvider around the routed Slot and ActionSelectionModal.

nodes.name: ActionSelectionModal.tsx
nodes.summary: Global 'Choose Action' modal for the native app that reads its visibility from ModalContext and offers Send and Request buttons, which set the jotai search category and push the /transfer route with the matching mode.

nodes.name: ActionSelectionModal
nodes.summary: Default-exported component that renders CustomModal styled from THEME; on Send or Request it calls selectCategoryAtom with SEARCH_CATEGORIES.SEND or REQUEST, closes the modal, and navigates to /transfer with a mode param.

nodes.name: CustomTabBar.tsx
nodes.summary: Custom bottom tab bar for the Expo Router tabs layout that renders Material icon tabs, filters out the search route, and inserts a raised green swap button at the midpoint that opens the action selection modal through ModalContext.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses react-native-copilot walkthroughable() and CopilotStep to make the center button a step in the guided app tour.

nodes.name: CustomTabBar
nodes.summary: Default-exported BottomTabBarProps component that maps visible routes to tabs via a nested renderTab helper (emits tabPress, navigates when not focused, picks icon and capitalized label) and calls setModalVisible(true) from the center button.

nodes.name: ModalContext.tsx
nodes.summary: React context module that holds a single boolean modalVisible flag and its setter, shared by the tab bar center button and the ActionSelectionModal so that one component can open the modal that the other renders.

nodes.name: ModalProvider
nodes.summary: Context provider component that stores modalVisible in useState (default false) and exposes the value and setModalVisible to its children; the root AppLayout mounts it around the whole app.

nodes.name: useModal
nodes.summary: Exported convenience hook that returns useContext(ModalContext), used by ActionSelectionModal to read modalVisible and call setModalVisible.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: ESLint flat config for the Expo React Native app that imports the shared array from packages/config/index.js and re-exports it unchanged via a spread.
nodes.languageNotes: ES module (.mjs) flat config; spreading the shared array leaves room to append app-specific config objects later.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: ESLint flat config for the NestJS user API workspace; it pulls in the monorepo's shared lint rules from packages/config/index.js and exports them as-is with no local overrides.

nodes.name: eslint.config.js
nodes.summary: Root-level ESLint flat config for the Yarn workspaces monorepo that loads the shared config array from ./packages/config/index.js and exports a spread copy for lint runs from the repo root.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Shared ESLint flat config array consumed by the root, apps/native, and apps/user eslint configs. It defines global ignores, a TypeScript/TSX block (typescript-eslint parser with existing tsconfig projects, react, react-hooks, import, prettier plugins), and a JS/JSX block parsed with espree, mostly at warn level.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses top-level await (`await import("espree")`) inside the exported array and filters tsconfig paths with fs.existsSync so missing workspaces do not break typed linting.

nodes.name: e2e-tests.config.ts
nodes.summary: Jest config for the NestJS user API end-to-end suite: it spreads the shared base config from jest.config.ts and sets testRegex to match only files ending in spec.e2e.ts.

nodes.name: int-tests.config.ts
nodes.summary: Jest config for the user API integration suite that reuses the base jest.config.ts settings and overrides testRegex so that only spec.int.ts files run.

nodes.name: jest.config.ts
nodes.summary: Base Jest config for the user API: it compiles .ts and .js files with ts-jest (using tsconfig.spec.json), runs tests in a node environment, and maps tsconfig.json path aliases to modules via pathsToModuleNameMapper. The unit, integration, and e2e configs spread this object and add their own testRegex.
nodes.languageNotes: It mixes an ES module default export with a CommonJS require() to load tsconfig.json as JSON. The displayName 'api' and the coverageDirectory '../../coverage/apps/api' look like they were left over from an earlier app name.

nodes.name: unit-tests.config.ts
nodes.summary: Jest config for the user API unit suite that extends the shared jest.config.ts and sets testRegex to 'spec.ts$'. That regex selects plain *.spec.ts unit test files.
nodes.languageNotes: The regex 'spec.ts$' has an unescaped dot and no anchor at the start, but it still excludes *.spec.e2e.ts and *.spec.int.ts files because those names end in 'e2e.ts' or 'int.ts'.

nodes.name: NotificationItem.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test that mounts NotificationItem with a mock notification (title, description, time "2h", thirdParty source) and asserts that the title, description, and time text render.

nodes.name: NotificationsList.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test that mounts NotificationsList with two mock notifications and checks that each title, description, and relative timestamp ("1h", "5h") appears in the rendered list.

nodes.name: NotificationItem.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side MUI component file for the web wallet that renders one selectable notification row with an initials avatar for the third-party source, plus a local getInitials helper that falls back to "?".
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Next.js "use client" directive and inline MUI sx props for selection highlight and transition styling.

nodes.name: NotificationsList.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side MUI component file that renders the web wallet notifications feed as a list of NotificationItem rows, or a wallet-icon empty state with a hint about recent transactions when the list is empty.

nodes.name: NotificationItem
nodes.summary: Exported React component that takes title, description, time, optional thirdParty, isSelected, and onSelect props, and renders a clickable row whose background turns #f8e4c4 when selected; NotificationsList renders one per notification.

nodes.name: NotificationsList
nodes.summary: Exported React component that takes a notifications array, keeps the selected index in useState, toggles selection on click via handleSelect, and maps each item to a NotificationItem or shows an empty-state message.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Jotai search state for the wallet: primitive atoms for query, loading, recent searches and selected category, derived atoms that filter and rank the mockData items into matching and non-matching sets, and write atoms (performSearchAtom, selectCategoryAtom, clearSearchAtom, startSearchAtom, cancelSearchAtom) that mutate that state. The useSearchResults hook consumes its derived atoms.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Jotai read-only derived atoms (atom(get => ...)) and write-only action atoms (atom(null, (get, set, arg) => ...)), with an explicit atom<null, [string], void> generic signature for typed write arguments.

nodes.name: sortSearchResults
nodes.summary: Returns a sorted copy of search items for a non-blank query: names that start with the query rank first, exact case-insensitive name matches rank next, and remaining ties sort alphabetically with localeCompare. matchingResultsAtom calls it after filterByQuery.

nodes.name: mockData.ts
nodes.summary: Exports a hard-coded mockData array of ten SearchItem records: five users in the send category and five businesses (including GreenStand) in the request category, some with a placeholder React Native logo avatar. The search atoms use it as the only data source for category filtering and query matching.

nodes.name: useSearchResults.ts
nodes.summary: React hook module that reads the search display, stats, selected-category and category-label atoms and turns them into SectionList-style sections for a search results screen.

nodes.name: useSearchResults
nodes.summary: Memoizes a SectionData array: an empty list when the query has no results, separate "Matching Results (n)" and "Other Results (n)" sections when a query is active, or one section titled with the category label and count otherwise. Returns sections, hasNoResults, selectedCategory and currentCategoryLabel.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the search domain types SearchItem, SectionData, SearchItemType (user or business) and SearchCategory (send, request or all), plus the SEARCH_CATEGORIES and SEARCH_TYPES constant maps. The search atoms, mockData and useSearchResults import these definitions.

nodes.name: TokenTree.cy.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component test that mounts TokenTree three ways and checks the data-test hooks: the photo src and species text with an image, the 'No photo' placeholder without one, and the 'Could not load' placeholder when hasError is set.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side Next.js App Router page at /token/details inside the protected route group that shows one token: its ID, wallet and creation date, its tree photo via TokenTree, an external map link, and its transaction history, all loaded through @treetracker/wallet hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: The default export wraps the inner component in React Suspense because useSearchParams requires a Suspense boundary in the Next.js App Router.

nodes.name: TokenDetails
nodes.summary: Reads the id and wallet query parameters, calls useGetToken, useGetTokenTransactions and useGetTokenTree, and renders MUI sections for token info, the TokenTree photo, a NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_URL map anchor, a back button to the wallet page, and a list of source-to-destination transactions.

nodes.name: TokenDetailsPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported Next.js page component that renders TokenDetails inside a Suspense boundary with a 'Loading…' Box fallback.

nodes.name: TokenTree.tsx
nodes.summary: Presentational MUI component module for the tree linked to a token, used by the token details page and covered by a Cypress component test; it exports only TokenTree and its optional Props type.

nodes.name: TokenTree
nodes.summary: Takes optional imageUrl, speciesName, isLoading and hasError props and renders a 160px box with the tree photo, or a placeholder text ('Loading…', 'Could not load the tree', or 'No photo for this tree'), plus the species name below when present.

nodes.name: login.cy.ts
nodes.summary: Cypress E2E spec for the web Login page: it loads the auth-data fixture, then checks successful login with sessionStorage token and redirect to home, rejection of invalid or short-username credentials, empty and short field validation, password visibility toggle, and the signup link.
nodes.languageNotes: Tests use function() callbacks instead of arrow functions so that this.authData (the cy.fixture alias) is reachable from the Mocha context.

nodes.name: signup.cy.ts
nodes.summary: Cypress E2E spec for the web Register page: it checks the form fields render, stubs POST **/register with cy.intercept to test a 200 success redirect to login and a 409 duplicate-user error, validates empty-field helper text, and checks the login link.

nodes.name: auth-constants.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Cypress support module for the login.cy.ts and signup.cy.ts specs: it exports the SELECTORS map of data-test ids for the auth forms and helper commands that fill the login and signup forms, assert errors and success, clear storage, and load the auth-data fixture.
nodes.languageNotes: SELECTORS uses 'as const' so every selector key keeps its literal string type; all helpers wrap the custom cy.getByData command.

nodes.name: loginWith
nodes.summary: Types the given username and password into the login-username and login-password fields and clicks the login submit button; login.cy.ts calls it for valid, invalid, and short-credential cases.

nodes.name: expectLoginError
nodes.summary: Asserts that the login-error element is visible and contains the given message; login.cy.ts uses it after failed credential attempts.

nodes.name: expectSuccessfulLogin
nodes.summary: Asserts that window.sessionStorage.token is a non-empty string, that the pathname equals the home route (default /home, 20 s timeout), and that the home-page element is visible.

nodes.name: registerWith
nodes.summary: Fills the signup form with the optional email, username, and confirmPassword values only when they are strings, always types the password, then clicks the signup submit button; signup.cy.ts calls it.

nodes.name: expectRegistrationSuccess
nodes.summary: Asserts that the signup-success element is visible and contains a message, by default 'User created successfully!'; no spec in this batch calls it.

nodes.name: expectValidationError
nodes.summary: Asserts that the element for an arbitrary data-test selector is visible and contains the given message; signup.cy.ts uses it for the 409 error and empty-field checks.

nodes.name: expectFormFieldError
nodes.summary: Asserts that the shared error-helper-text element is visible and contains the given field validation message; login.cy.ts uses it for empty and short field checks.

nodes.name: generateUniqueEmail
nodes.summary: Returns a unique test email address of the form testuser<Date.now()>@example.com so that signup.cy.ts can register a new user without collisions.

nodes.name: clearAuthSession
nodes.summary: Clears both sessionStorage and localStorage of the application window to reset any stored auth state between tests.

nodes.name: loadAuthFixture
nodes.summary: Loads the auth-data fixture with cy.fixture and aliases it as authData, which both specs read as this.authData for routes, users, and error messages.

nodes.name: getFixtureData
nodes.summary: Reads the authData alias and resolves a dot-separated path (for example 'users.validUser') against it with split and reduce, yielding the nested fixture value.

nodes.name: commands.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the custom Cypress commands login and logout for the web app tests: login POSTs TEST_USER credentials (default demo/demodemon) to the api_server /login endpoint, asserts HTTP 200, and stores access_token in sessionStorage under "token"; logout removes that key. Also augments the global Cypress.Chainable type with both commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript declaration merging (declare global + namespace Cypress) so custom commands are type-checked on cy, and export {} to make the file a module.

nodes.name: component.tsx
nodes.summary: Cypress component-testing support file loaded before each component spec; it side-effect imports ./commands and registers cy.mount from cypress/react so specs can render React components, with a matching Chainable type augmentation.

nodes.name: e2e.ts
nodes.summary: Cypress end-to-end support file loaded before each E2E spec; it side-effect imports ./commands and adds the getByData command, which selects elements by their data-test attribute, plus its Chainable type declaration.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Next.js App Router handler for POST /api/auth/signup that reads username, email, and password from the JSON body and calls createUser from userService to register the user in Keycloak.
nodes.languageNotes: Next.js App Router convention: a route.ts file exports functions named after HTTP methods (here POST) to define API endpoints.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Parses the signup request body, delegates to createUser, and maps the result to a NextResponse with status 201 on success, 409 when the user exists, or 500 with the error message on an exception.

nodes.name: tokenService.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side helper that obtains a Keycloak admin access token from the master realm with the OAuth2 password grant, using admin credentials from NEXT_PUBLIC_KEYCLOAK_* environment variables; userService uses it before admin API calls.
nodes.languageNotes: The admin credentials are read from NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed env vars, which Next.js inlines into client bundles if this module is ever imported from client code.

nodes.name: getToken
nodes.summary: POSTs a form-encoded password-grant request to the Keycloak master realm openid-connect token endpoint and returns the access_token string, or throws an Error with the response text when the request fails.

nodes.name: userService.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side service that creates wallet users in Keycloak through the admin REST API, authenticating with a token from tokenService; the signup API route calls its createUser export.

nodes.name: createUser
nodes.summary: Gets an admin token via getToken, POSTs an enabled user with a non-temporary password credential to the Keycloak admin users endpoint for the configured realm, and returns success on 201, a user-exists failure on 409, or throws on other statuses.

nodes.name: DateRangeInput.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side React component file for the web wallet that exports DateRangeInput, a pair of MUI date fields used by WalletFiltersModal to pick a custom start and end date.

nodes.name: DateRangeInput
nodes.summary: Renders side-by-side 'From' and 'To' MUI TextFields of type date with shrunk labels and aria labels, reporting each new string value through the onChangeStart and onChangeEnd callbacks.

nodes.name: RadioButton.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side React component file that exports RadioButton, a labeled MUI radio wrapper that WalletFiltersModal uses for each preset date filter option.

nodes.name: RadioButton
nodes.summary: Renders a single MUI FormControlLabel with a controlled Radio inside a padded Box, taking label, value, checked and an argument-less onChange handler, and reusing the label as the aria label.

nodes.name: WalletFiltersModal.tsx
nodes.summary: Defines the web wallet's bottom-sheet filters dialog and its WalletFilterOption and WalletFiltersValue types, composing RadioButton presets and a DateRangeInput to build a date filter value.
nodes.languageNotes: The component is fully controlled: it holds no state and emits a new immutable WalletFiltersValue object via spread on every change.

nodes.name: WalletFiltersModal
nodes.summary: Renders an MUI Dialog styled as a rounded bottom sheet with a close button, four date-preset radios (all, past 90 days, May, 2024), a custom date range, and an Apply button; it emits changes via onChange and the final value via onApply.

nodes.name: wallet.ts
nodes.summary: Mock wallet API for the shared core package that uses @faker-js/faker to generate fake Wallet records with random Received/Pending/Sent status and signed balances, after a simulated 100 ms network delay. It exports getWalletsRecentActivity and getWalletByKeyword, and the useWalletList hook consumes it.
nodes.languageNotes: Async functions await a setTimeout-based Promise to imitate network latency; status values use a string literal union type.

nodes.name: getWalletsRecentActivity
nodes.summary: Waits 100 ms, then returns four freshly generated fake Wallet objects (uuid id, faker username, logo URL, past createdAt, random status, and a balance that is negative when the status is Sent). It accepts a userId argument but ignores it, and useWalletList calls it to load the recent-activity list.

nodes.name: getWalletByKeyword
nodes.summary: Waits 100 ms, then filters a module-level list of ten pre-generated fake wallets and returns those whose name contains the keyword, compared case-insensitively. It acts as a mock wallet search endpoint.

nodes.name: wallet.ts
nodes.summary: React hook module in the shared core package that default-exports useWalletList, which loads wallet recent activity from the core mock wallet API and exposes the list with a loading flag.

nodes.name: useWalletList
nodes.summary: Holds a Wallet[] list and an isWalletLoading flag in useState, and on mount runs a useEffect that calls getWalletsRecentActivity with the userId (or an empty string) and stores the result. It returns { list, isWalletLoading }; the effect has an empty dependency array, so a userId change does not trigger a reload.

nodes.name: wallet.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the shared Wallet type (id, name, logo, numeric balance, createdAt Date, and status string) that the core wallet API and the useWalletList hook use as their data shape.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list for the NestJS user API image, keeping node_modules, dist, deployment, .git, .cache, .env, .github and .husky out of the context sent to apps/user/Dockerfile.
nodes.languageNotes: Excluding .env keeps local secrets out of the image layers, and excluding node_modules and dist forces the builder stage to install and compile from a clean state.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Two-stage node:18-alpine build for the NestJS user API: the builder stage runs yarn install and yarn build and then prunes to production dependencies, and the prod stage copies dist and node_modules, exposes port 8080 and starts node dist/src/main.js.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build: only the compiled dist folder and the pruned production node_modules reach the final image. The builder copies only package.json before yarn install (no yarn.lock), so dependency versions are not pinned by a lockfile inside this build context.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Builder stage on node:18-alpine that installs all dependencies from package.json, compiles the user API with yarn build, and reinstalls with --production --ignore-scripts to leave only runtime packages in /app/node_modules.

nodes.name: prod
nodes.summary: Runtime stage on node:18-alpine that takes app/dist and app/node_modules from the builder stage, exposes port 8080, and runs the compiled NestJS bootstrap file dist/src/main.js.

nodes.name: build-dev-docker-img-and-relase.yml
nodes.summary: Release workflow that runs on every push to main in the Greenstand repo (unless the commit says skip ci), installs Yarn dependencies on Node 24.10.0, and runs semantic-release with the commit-analyzer, changelog, npm, git and GitHub plugins to tag versions and publish release notes. Despite the file name, it builds no Docker image.
nodes.languageNotes: fetch-depth: 0 gives semantic-release the full git history and tags it needs to compute the next version.

nodes.name: ci-cd-deploy-web-prod.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that writes production NEXT_PUBLIC_* values (Keycloak, wallet API, user API, map and query URLs) into apps/web/.env.production, builds the Next.js static export, then syncs apps/web/out to the production S3 bucket and invalidates the CloudFront distribution for wallet.treetracker.org.
nodes.languageNotes: Two jobs pass the static build through upload-artifact and download-artifact; the deploy job runs only in the Greenstand/treetracker-wallet-app repository.

nodes.name: ci-cd-deploy-web-test.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that builds the apps/web Next.js static export with only DEPLOYMENT_HOSTNAME set in .env.production, then syncs the out directory to the test S3 bucket and invalidates CloudFront for wallet-test.treetracker.org.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-bdd-android.yml
nodes.summary: Android end-to-end workflow for PRs that touch apps/bdd, apps/native, packages/core or packages/wallet (and for pushes to main). It caches Gradle, the AVD, the Expo prebuild and the debug APK, embeds the JS bundle, starts the user service on port 8080, installs Appium 3 with UiAutomator2, and runs yarn bdd:test:android:report (wdio.mobile.conf.ts) on an API 34 emulator. A second job publishes the Cucumber HTML report to gh-pages under webdriver/android and upserts a PR comment with the report links.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses actions/cache cache-hit outputs to skip the prebuild and the APK build, and an HTML-comment marker so that github-script updates one PR comment instead of adding new ones.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-bdd-wallet.yml
nodes.summary: Web BDD end-to-end workflow that runs on pull_request_target for changes in apps/bdd, apps/web, apps/user, packages/core or packages/wallet (and on pushes to main). It builds the web static export, serves apps/web/out on port 3000, starts the user service on port 8080, runs yarn bdd:test:web:report (WebdriverIO with wdio.web.conf.ts), publishes the Cucumber report to gh-pages under webdriver/web, and pins one de-duplicated report-link comment on the PR.
nodes.languageNotes: pull_request_target with an explicit PR-head checkout gives secrets to same-repo PRs; the job-level if guard skips fork PRs.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-package-queue.yml
nodes.summary: PR workflow for changes under packages/queue (excluding Markdown) that checks out the PR head for same-repo PRs, installs the monorepo with Yarn on Node 20, and runs yarn workspace queue test (Jest on __tests__/index.spec.js) against the DATABASE_URL secret.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-queue-package-wallet.yml
nodes.summary: Older, near-duplicate queue package workflow (its header comment wrongly says wallet package) that installs packages/queue in isolation with npm install --no-workspaces --legacy-peer-deps and runs npm run test with DATABASE_URL. Unlike ci-cd-pr-package-queue.yml, it has no fork guard.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-user-wallet.yml
nodes.summary: PR workflow for non-Markdown changes in apps/user that installs dependencies with Yarn on Node 20 and runs the NestJS user service unit tests, integration tests, and e2e tests (yarn user:test:unit, user:test:int, user:test:e2e --forceExit) with Keycloak, database and wallet API secrets.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-wallet-package-wallet.yml
nodes.summary: PR workflow for changes in packages/wallet and its dependencies packages/keycloak and packages/core that runs yarn workspace @treetracker/wallet test (Jest) with Keycloak secrets and the NEXT_PUBLIC_TREETRACKER_WALLET_API variable.

nodes.name: ci-cd-pr-web-wallet.yml
nodes.summary: PR workflow for non-Markdown changes in apps/web that starts the user service on port 8080 in the background and then runs the Cypress component tests and headless Cypress e2e tests through cypress-io/github-action.

nodes.name: pr-ci-cd-all.yml
nodes.summary: Repository-wide quality gate for every pull request and every push to main: it runs the Prettier check (yarn format --check), lint-staged with Prettier and ESLint, and commitlint on the subject of the last commit.

nodes.name: static-website-deploy-dev.yml
nodes.summary: Dev deployment workflow that runs on pushes to main that touch apps/web (or on manual dispatch, unless the commit says skip-ci). It writes dev NEXT_PUBLIC_* endpoints into apps/web/.env.local, builds the Next.js static export, syncs it to the dev S3 bucket, and invalidates CloudFront for wallet-dev.treetracker.org.

nodes.name: .yarnrc.yml
nodes.summary: Yarn Berry settings file with one key, nodeLinker: node-modules, so Yarn 4 installs workspace dependencies into classic node_modules folders instead of Plug'n'Play.
nodes.languageNotes: Yarn 4 defaults to Plug'n'Play; the node-modules linker keeps compatibility with tools such as Expo, Metro and Next.js that expect a node_modules tree.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Generated conventional-commits release notes for version 1.0.0 (2025-12-13), with Bug Fixes, Features and Reverts lists that link commits for the web, native, user API, BDD, queue and shared config work.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
