nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview for the Greenstand Treetracker Wallet App: prerequisites, env file setup, root yarn scripts for web, native and user API development, the WebdriverIO BDD test commands and debug workflow, the monorepo structure, Corepack Yarn 4 notes and links to the contributing guide.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Root Yarn 4.9.4 workspaces manifest (apps/*, packages/*) that defines the delegating scripts for web, native, user, Cypress and @treetracker/bdd workspaces, plus lint, Prettier format, type-check and husky hooks, and the shared ESLint, TypeScript and commitlint devDependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: Scripts use `yarn workspace <name> run <script>` so all app commands run from the repository root.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Root TypeScript solution file with no own files and project references to apps/web, apps/native, apps/user and packages/core; the root type-check script runs `tsc --build` on it.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript project references (composite build); apps/wallets and packages/keycloak references are commented out.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template env file for the BDD package that declares empty PROJECT_ROOT_ANDROID and PROJECT_ROOT_IOS variables, which utils/capabilities.ts reads to locate the native app builds for Appium mobile runs.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Main guide for the WebdriverIO + Cucumber BDD package: quick start, the scripts/watch.ts test watcher (keyboard commands, CLI flags, smart spec detection), the yarn test and report scripts, the folder layout, the four wdio.*.conf.ts configs, step-definition examples, and troubleshooting.

nodes.name: bdd-testing.md
nodes.summary: How-to for running the BDD suite on Web and Android and producing Cucumber HTML reports: prerequisites (web:dev, user:dev, emulator, Appium), the bdd:test:web:report and bdd:test:android:report commands, and the report paths under test-artifacts/reports.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Manifest of the private ESM @treetracker/bdd workspace: defines wdio scripts for web, debug, Android and iOS runs, per-feature runs, report generation and the tsx watcher, with WebdriverIO, Cucumber, Appium, msw and pg dev dependencies plus workspace links to keycloak, wallet and core.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript settings for the BDD package: strict NodeNext ES2022 type-check only (noEmit, noImplicitAny off), @wdio/globals types, ts-node transpileOnly, and path aliases to the keycloak and wallet packages for all features, mocks and support .ts files.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Environment template for the native app that is not empty: it holds a single PROJECT_ROOT= key with no value and no trailing newline, which is why the scanner reports 0 lines.
nodes.languageNotes: The file has 13 bytes and no newline, so line counters such as wc -l report 0 lines although one variable is defined.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step guide for running Appium-based BDD tests of the Expo native app on an Android emulator and an iOS simulator, covering Appium 3 drivers, prebuild, native builds, PROJECT_ROOT_ANDROID and PROJECT_ROOT_IOS in bdd/.env, Metro startup and the bdd:test commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Several commands in the guide (yarn build-apk-android, yarn build-app-ios) do not match the script names in apps/native/package.json (build-android, build-ios).

nodes.name: app.json
nodes.summary: Expo app manifest for the wallet mobile app: it sets the com.gtw.app bundle ID and package, the myapp URL scheme, icons and the green splash screen, enables the New Architecture and the React Compiler, and registers expo-router, expo-font, expo-camera, expo-image-picker and expo-dev-client plugins with QR-scanning permission texts.
nodes.languageNotes: app.config.js receives this manifest as config and replaces its plugins array with only expo-web-browser and expo-router, so the camera, image-picker and dev-client plugin settings here can be overridden at build time.

nodes.name: eas.json
nodes.summary: EAS Build profiles for the native app: a development profile that builds an internal APK with expo-dev-client, a preview profile that builds a clean internal APK for QA and CI, and a production profile that builds an Android app bundle for Google Play.
nodes.languageNotes: The file uses JSONC comments, which EAS accepts but strict JSON parsers reject.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest of the Expo React Native app: it sets expo-router/entry as the main entry, defines scripts for Expo start and prebuild, native Gradle and xcodebuild builds, WebdriverIO and Appium E2E runs, Maestro tests, Jest, ESLint and Prettier, and declares Expo 54, React Native 0.81, jotai, react-native-paper and the shared core workspace package.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration for the native app that extends expo/tsconfig.base, uses react-native JSX, turns on strict mode but turns off strictNullChecks, and maps path aliases such as @app, @components, @common, @hooks, @utils and @/ to local folders.
nodes.languageNotes: The strict flag is on, but strictNullChecks is explicitly off, so null and undefined checks are not enforced.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template of environment variables for the NestJS user API: Keycloak realm, base URL, client ID and secret, DATABASE_URL, the wallet API key, and production and dev CORS origin lists (dev defaults to localhost:3000/3001). Developers copy it to .env before they run the server or the tests.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for the user API: it documents the POST /register endpoint with a curl example, the Swagger UI at localhost:8080/swagger, and the e2e, integration and unit test commands. It also explains how to set up a Keycloak realm role (wallet-operator-microservice) so that a client-credentials token from this service can call the wallet API, and how to create .env from .env.example.

nodes.name: nest-cli.json
nodes.summary: Nest CLI configuration that uses the @nestjs/schematics collection, sets src as the source root, and points the build entry file at apps/user/src/main. The nest build and nest start scripts read it.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest for the private "user" NestJS 9 API package. It defines build, start (dev, debug, prod via node dist/src/main), lint, and Jest test scripts (unit, e2e and integration configs), and declares NestJS, Swagger, axios and class-validator runtime dependencies plus the @treetracker/config shared dev package.

nodes.name: tsconfig.build.json
nodes.summary: Production build TypeScript config that extends the base user API tsconfig and excludes node_modules, dist, test folders, and all *.spec.ts, *.test.ts and __tests__ files, so nest build compiles only application sources.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Base TypeScript compiler config for the user API: CommonJS output to ./dist targeting ES2017, decorator metadata enabled for NestJS dependency injection, loose strictness (no strictNullChecks or noImplicitAny), and path aliases @utils/*, @dtos/* and @packages/* that the source files use for shared libs.
nodes.languageNotes: emitDecoratorMetadata and experimentalDecorators are required for NestJS, because its injector reads constructor parameter types from reflect-metadata at runtime.

nodes.name: tsconfig.spec.json
nodes.summary: Test-only TypeScript config that extends the base tsconfig, emits to ../../dist/out-tsc with jest types, and includes jest.config.ts together with all *.test.ts, *.spec.ts and *.d.ts files for the Jest suites.

nodes.name: cluster-role-binding.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes ClusterRoleBinding that grants the k8s-wait-for ClusterRole to the default ServiceAccount in the treetracker-wallet-monorepo-user-api namespace, so user API pods can read services, pods and jobs.

nodes.name: cluster-role.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes ClusterRole named k8s-wait-for that allows get, watch and list on services, pods and jobs in the core and batch API groups, which is the permission set the k8s-wait-for init pattern needs.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Deployment that runs 2 replicas of the greenstand/treetracker-wallet-monorepo-user-api image on container port 8080, pinned by node affinity to the DigitalOcean microservices-node-pool; the TAG placeholder in the image name is replaced per environment.
nodes.languageNotes: The image tag is the literal placeholder TAG, so a Kustomize overlay or the release pipeline must set the real tag.

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize base for the NestJS user API that lists the six manifests of this directory (Deployment, Ambassador Mapping, Service, Namespace, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding) so environment overlays can build on them.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Ambassador getambassador.io/v2 Mapping that routes requests with the /user-api/ path prefix to the treetracker-wallet-monorepo-user-api-service Kubernetes Service.

nodes.name: namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Namespace manifest that creates the treetracker-wallet-monorepo-user-api namespace, which holds the user API Deployment and Service.

nodes.name: service.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes ClusterIP Service named treetracker-wallet-monorepo-user-api-service that selects the user API pods by label and maps TCP port 80 to container port 8080.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template of environment variables for the Next.js web app: user and wallet API base URLs, API timeout and retry counts, the app base URL, Keycloak URL, realm and client ID, the map and query API URLs, and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for dev TLS. The Keycloak values feed the client setup in src/auth/keycloak.ts.
nodes.languageNotes: All browser-visible variables use the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix so that Next.js inlines them into the client bundle. The last three lines put spaces around '=', which many dotenv parsers handle differently from the other lines.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Short guide for the Treetracker Wallet Next.js web app: an overview, a feature list for token send and receive, steps to clone, run `yarn` at the root and `yarn dev` in apps/web on localhost:3000, and the Cypress scripts for component and integration tests. It notes that E2E testing moved to the BDD package in apps/bdd.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest for the private 'web' package (version 5.0.0): it defines Next.js dev, build and start scripts (dev and start also run the wallet_state loadEnv script), ESLint and Prettier scripts, and Cypress component and E2E scripts through start-server-and-test. Dependencies include Next 15, React 19, MUI 6 with Emotion, Jotai, keycloak-js 18, qrcode.react, and the internal @treetracker/wallet and core packages.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'dev' and 'start' scripts chain 'next dev && yarn workspace wallet_state loadEnv', so the loadEnv step runs only after the long-running Next.js server exits.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration for the web app that extends the shared @treetracker/config base and sets strict, noEmit, ES2017 target, bundler module resolution, preserved JSX, and the Next.js language-service plugin. It maps the '@/*' alias to './src/*' and includes all .ts and .tsx files plus the generated .next/types.

nodes.name: auth-data.json
nodes.summary: Cypress fixture holding login users (valid, invalid, short password, short username), signup payloads, expected login and registration error messages, and the /login, /signup, /home routes. The loadAuthFixture helper in support/auth-constants.ts aliases it as authData for the login.cy.ts and signup.cy.ts E2E specs.

nodes.name: example.json
nodes.summary: Default Cypress scaffold fixture with placeholder name, email, and body strings. No spec or support file under apps/web/cypress loads it, so it is unused sample data.

nodes.name: wallet.json
nodes.summary: Cypress fixture for the wallet creation flow: the /wallet route, an empty initial wallet list mock, a created wallet mock (wallet_123, My Test Wallet), and the duplicate-name error text. The create-wallet.cy.ts E2E spec loads it directly, and loadWalletFixture in support/wallet-constants.ts also aliases it as walletData.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Manifest for the private @treetracker/config ESM workspace package. It exposes the shared ESLint flat config (index.js) as './eslint', the base './tsconfig.json', and the Prettier rules as './prettier', and declares the typescript-eslint, import, react, react-hooks and eslint-config-prettier plugins as peer dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'exports' map is a Node.js package subpath export, so consumers import '@treetracker/config/eslint' instead of a file path; peerDependencies make each consuming workspace install the ESLint plugins itself.

nodes.name: prettier.config.json
nodes.summary: Repo-wide Prettier formatting rules: 80-column print width, 2-space indentation without tabs, double quotes, trailing commas everywhere, arrows without parentheses for single params, and JSX closing brackets on the same line. The root 'format' and 'format:check' scripts and lint-staged pass it to Prettier via --config.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Shared base TypeScript compiler settings (ES2020 target, CommonJS modules, strict mode, esModuleInterop, skipLibCheck, consistent file-name casing) that include src and types folders and exclude node_modules and dist. The web app tsconfig extends it through the '@treetracker/config/tsconfig.json' package export.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template listing the four empty PRIVATE_KEYCLOAK_* variables (realm, base URL, client ID, client secret) that the keycloak package's Node.js config reads via dotenv when running its tests.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Usage guide for @treetracker/keycloak covering Node.js .env and Expo extra-field configuration, examples for fetchTokenFromKeycloak and deleteAccountFromKeycloak, an API reference with return types, and how to run the e2e tests.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest that names the @treetracker/keycloak package, points its main entry at ./src/index.ts so consumers load TypeScript source directly, and wires the test script to Jest 28 with ts-jest and ts-node dev dependencies.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript compiler settings for the keycloak package: CommonJS output to ./dist targeting ES2017 with declarations and source maps, relaxed strictness, node and jest types, and path aliases mapping @treetracker/keycloak and @packages/keycloak to ./src.

nodes.name: tsconfig.spec.json

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what the Treetracker Wallet App is: a Greenstand wallet for managing and transferring tokens that represent verified tree planting. It explains the prerequisites, the env files each workspace needs, and the root yarn scripts that start the web app, the native app and the user API. The root package.json defines the Yarn 4 workspaces (apps/* and packages/*) and the delegating scripts, and CONTRIBUTING.md describes the monorepo layout, the per-app tech stacks and the Conventional Commits rules that the rest of this tour refers to.

tour.title: Shared Auth State
tour.description: The @treetracker/core package is the foundation that both client apps share, so it comes before any app code. Its index re-exports the Jotai auth atoms: tokenAtom persists the auth token, and getAsyncStorage picks sessionStorage on web or AsyncStorage on native, so one atom works on both platforms. Write-only atoms such as loginAtom validate form input with Joi before they call the user API, and every wallet hook later in this tour reads its auth token from tokenAtom.
tour.languageLesson: Jotai models state as small atoms. A primitive atom holds a value, atomWithStorage persists that value through a storage adapter, and a write-only atom (created with a null read function) acts like an action that can read and set other atoms.

tour.title: Wallet Client Foundations
tour.description: The @treetracker/wallet package is the client for the Greenstand wallet API, and its barrel index has the largest fan-out in the graph because it re-exports every API client, hook and type. The shared types in types/wallet.ts (Wallet, Transfer, ActionTokenSummary, Transaction) mirror the wallet API responses, and utils/config.ts, the most depended-upon file in the project, resolves the API base URLs from NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables on web or from Expo Constants on native. The typed WalletApiError in errors.ts carries the server reason slug, so callers can branch on cases such as no_wallet without parsing message text.
tour.languageLesson: A TypeScript barrel file uses 'export * from' or named re-exports to give a package one public import path. Consumers import from the package root, and the internal folder structure can change without breaking them.

tour.title: Wallet API Clients and Hooks
tour.description: Each wallet feature is a pair: an API client function that calls one wallet API endpoint, and a React hook that binds it to the tokenAtom from Step 2. createWallet and useCreateWallet show the thin pattern, and sendTransfer starts a transfer of specific tokens or of an N-token bundle. usePendingTransfers adds list state plus accept, decline and cancel actions, and redeemActionToken turns a share link into a completed transfer. The web pages in Steps 6 and 7 are built almost entirely from these hooks.
tour.languageLesson: A custom React hook is a function whose name starts with 'use' and that calls other hooks. Here the hooks read the auth token from the core tokenAtom and call the matching API client, so a page component gets data, loading state and actions from one call without knowing about HTTP or auth.

tour.title: Web App Root and Keycloak
tour.description: The Next.js web wallet starts at the App Router root layout, which wraps every page in the MUI theme and the KeycloakProvider. The provider waits for an 8-second capped Keycloak init, mirrors the access token into the core tokenAtom from Step 2, and refreshes it on expiry, while auth/keycloak.ts wraps keycloak-js with an idempotent PKCE init. The root page and the /auth/callback page read the authenticated flag from the useAuth hook and redirect to /home or /login. These files form a tightly coupled cluster in the graph, so they are best read together.
tour.languageLesson: React context lets a provider near the root share a value with any descendant. KeycloakProvider exposes ready and authenticated through a useAuth hook, and it blocks rendering until init finishes, so no child page renders with an unknown auth state.

tour.title: Protected Routes and Navigation
tour.description: Next.js route groups split the web app into (public) and (protected) areas without changing URLs. The protected layout is the client-side auth gate: it redirects to /login when tokenAtom is empty or when another tab broadcasts logout through the BroadcastChannel in sessionChannel.ts. It also wraps pages in the header and snackbar contexts and in the bottom navigation bar, which badges the Notifications tab with the incoming transfer count from the wallet hooks of Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, a folder name in parentheses, such as (protected), is a route group. It shares a layout among its pages but does not add a URL segment, so /home stays /home.

tour.title: Web Wallet Features
tour.description: These pages show the main token flows of the web wallet, all built on the hooks from Step 4. The home page shows token and wallet totals plus recent activity, the wallet page lists and creates wallets, and the send page sends tokens to a named wallet or generates a claim link with a QR code. The transfers page groups incoming, outgoing and share-link items with accept, decline and cancel actions, and the public /claim page redeems a shared link or saves it until the user signs in and has a wallet.

tour.title: Native App Shell
tour.description: The Expo React Native app uses Expo Router, so the folder structure under apps/native/app defines the routes, much like the web App Router from Step 5. The root _layout.tsx waits for the Roboto fonts and renders every route inside ModalProvider together with the global ActionSelectionModal, a cluster the graph also detects. The index route sends first-time users to onboarding, signed-in users to the home tab and everyone else to login, and the (tabs) layout declares the home, wallet, notifications and settings tabs.
tour.languageLesson: Expo Router is file-based routing for React Native. A _layout.tsx file wraps the routes in its folder (Slot, Stack or Tabs), a folder name in parentheses is a group that does not appear in the URL, and [walletId].tsx is a dynamic route.

tour.title: Native Screens and Design Tokens
tour.description: The home tab screen shows balance cards and a recent-activity list, and it swaps to search results while the core search state is active. That search state lives in the core package: Jotai atoms for the query and the send or request category, plus derived atoms that rank the matching items. Every screen shares the HeaderSearch bar, and the design tokens in theme/index.ts and constants/Colors.ts (among the most imported native files) define the Greenstand greens, spacing and Roboto typography. Note that much of the native data is still mock data, unlike the web app, which already uses the wallet hooks.

tour.title: User API Bootstrap
tour.description: The NestJS user API is the backend that the client apps call for login and registration. main.ts bootstraps AppModule, enables Swagger outside production, applies a whitelisting ValidationPipe and CORS, and listens on port 8080. AppModule wires the user, auth and queue modules, UserController exposes POST /login, POST /register, GET /healthz and GET /me, and RegisterUserDto validates the registration body. The OpenAPI spec under docs/api documents the register endpoint contract.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS uses TypeScript decorators and dependency injection. @Module groups providers and controllers, @Controller and @Post map methods to routes, and class-validator decorators on a DTO class let the global ValidationPipe reject bad request bodies before the controller runs.

tour.title: Keycloak Identity Integration
tour.description: Keycloak is the identity provider for the whole system. In the user API, UserService proxies login, user creation and profile lookup to Keycloak, and AuthService gets a service-account token with the client_credentials grant and caches it until it expires. The separate @treetracker/keycloak package offers the same kind of admin helpers (token fetch, account create and delete) for Node code such as the BDD seed in Step 13. Together with the KeycloakProvider from Step 5, these files show how one Keycloak realm serves the browser and the servers.

tour.title: Wallet Creation Queue
tour.description: When a new wallet is created, the user API reacts through a PostgreSQL message queue instead of a direct HTTP call. QueueListenerService registers a callback at module init, onQueueNotification subscribes to the wallets/creation channel, and for each account_id the service transfers a reward token bundle to the new wallet with the AuthService token from Step 11. The queue package implements this pub/sub: publish inserts a row into queue.message, and subscribe issues LISTEN and acknowledges each row. This is the deepest path of the BFS from the user API entry point.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY is a built-in pub/sub mechanism. A client runs LISTEN on a channel and receives a notification when another session runs NOTIFY, so services can react to database events without polling. Storing each message in a table and recording an ack, as this package does, adds a durable record of delivery.

tour.title: BDD and Component Testing
tour.description: The project tests user journeys end to end with WebdriverIO and Cucumber in apps/bdd. Gherkin features such as send-token.feature describe accept, decline and cancel transfer scenarios in plain language, steps.ts implements them against the running web app, and seed.ts recreates fixed Keycloak users, wallets and tokens so each run starts from a known state. The shared wdio.base.conf.ts configures reporters, videos and failure screenshots, and cypress.config.ts sets up the separate Cypress component and E2E tests of the web app.
tour.languageLesson: Gherkin writes tests as Given/When/Then scenarios. Each step line matches a step definition function by text or regular expression, and tags such as @web or @skip let the runner select which scenarios execute.

tour.title: Containers and Kubernetes
tour.description: The user API from Steps 10 to 12 ships as a container image. The Dockerfile uses a node:18-alpine builder stage to install, compile and prune dependencies, and a prod stage that copies only dist and node_modules and runs dist/src/main.js on port 8080. The Kustomize base lists the Kubernetes manifests: a Deployment with two replicas and an Ambassador Mapping that routes the /user-api/ prefix to the service, and the development overlay patches that Mapping with CORS settings.
tour.languageLesson: Kustomize builds Kubernetes YAML without templates. A base directory lists shared manifests, and an overlay references the base and applies patches, such as a changed Mapping, for one environment.

tour.title: CI/CD and Releases
tour.description: GitHub Actions ties the tour together. pr-ci-cd-all.yml checks formatting, lint and commit messages on every pull request, and ci-cd-pr-bdd-wallet.yml builds the web static export, starts the user API and runs the BDD suite from Step 13, then publishes the Cucumber report. static-website-deploy-dev.yml syncs the web export to S3 behind CloudFront, and the release workflow runs semantic-release with .releaserc.js to tag versions and update the changelog from Conventional Commits.
tour.languageLesson: A GitHub Actions workflow declares 'on' triggers (pull_request, push, workflow_dispatch), 'paths' filters to run only when relevant folders change, and 'jobs' made of sequential 'steps'. semantic-release reads Conventional Commit messages to choose the next version number.
